content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent follow-up duration statements",
      "quote": "until all patients have had the opportunity for approximately 44 weeks of follow-up after treatment assignment. This will provide at least 6 months of follow-up from the anticipated median time of first response assessment.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis states 44 weeks of follow-up, but later in the same section it says the final analysis for DoR is planned when the last patient has had approximately 32 weeks of follow-up. These two durations are inconsistent and could lead to confusion about the actual follow-up period.",
      "fix": "Clarify the exact follow-up duration for the final analysis and ensure consistency between the overall follow-up and the DoR analysis timepoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Cross-reference to non-existent section",
      "quote": "Intervention after the end of the study is described in Section 99.7.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The text references Section 99.7, which does not exist in the protocol. This is a broken cross-reference that leaves the reader without information on post-study access to the intervention.",
      "fix": "Replace 'Section 99.7' with the correct section number that describes post-study access, or add that section if missing."
    },
    {
      "title": "Interim futility evaluation details incomplete",
      "quote": "Enrolment in a specific tumor type will be paused after 8 patients with Investigator-assessed measurable disease at baseline have been treated within that tumor type, until a decision has been made on whether to stop enrolment to that tumor type based on the interim futility evaluation.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis mentions an interim futility evaluation but does not specify the statistical method, the decision rules beyond the observed response, or the timing. It also refers to 'Section 9.4.6' for further details, but that section is not provided in the text.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed description of the interim futility evaluation, including the statistical design, decision rules, and timing, and ensure the referenced section exists."
    },
    {
      "title": "Contraception requirements not specified",
      "quote": "T-DXd will be administered to patients harboring tumors with specific HER2 activating mutations at a dose of 5.4 mg/kg via IV infusion on Day 1 of each cycle, every 3 weeks (q3w).",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not include any contraception requirements for patients, which is a critical safety element for a drug like T-DXd that may have teratogenic potential. The M11 template requires a dedicated section on contraception.",
      "fix": "Add a section detailing contraception requirements for both male and female patients, including duration and acceptable methods."
    },
    {
      "title": "No Data Monitoring Committee but interim futility planned",
      "quote": "There will be no Data Monitoring Committee for this study.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis states there is no DMC, yet the protocol describes interim futility evaluations that require independent review of unblinded data. Without a DMC, it is unclear who will perform these evaluations and how bias will be avoided.",
      "fix": "Clarify the oversight mechanism for interim futility evaluations, either by establishing a DMC or describing an alternative independent review process."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint definition lacks central review details",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint is confirmed ORR assessed by ICR per RECIST v1.1 across all tumor types.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The synopsis does not specify how the independent central review (ICR) will be conducted, including the number of readers, adjudication process, or timing. This is important for reproducibility and consistency.",
      "fix": "Add a description of the ICR methodology, including reader qualifications, blinding, and adjudication procedures."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size rationale lacks precision for tumor type caps",
      "quote": "Approximately 100 patients will be treated in this study, with a maximum of approximately 20 patients per tumor type to ensure adequate representation across multiple tumor types.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The sample size justification does not explain how the 20-patient cap per tumor type was determined or how it affects the precision of the overall ORR estimate. The statistical rationale is incomplete.",
      "fix": "Provide a more detailed sample size calculation that accounts for the tumor type caps and the expected distribution of patients across types."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent use of 'enrolled' and 'treated'",
      "quote": "this study will enrol and screen 130 patients to achieve a global target of 100 patients treated with T-DXd.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "1.1 Synopsis",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The synopsis uses 'enrol and screen' together, but later defines 'enrolled' as consent to participate, which is different from being screened. This could cause confusion about the actual number of patients needed.",
      "fix": "Clarify the definitions of 'enrolled', 'screened', and 'treated' and use them consistently throughout the protocol."
    }
  ]
}
